A refrigerator keeps food cold by using a continuous cycle of evaporation and condensation to move heat from the inside of the unit to the outside. A substance called a **refrigerant** flows through coils; as it travels through the evaporator coils inside the fridge, it absorbs heat from the food and surrounding air, causing the refrigerant to evaporate into a gas. This gas is then compressed by a compressor, which increases its temperature and pressure, and then flows through condenser coils on the outside of the unit where it releases the heat into the room and turns back into a liquid. This cycle repeats, constantly "pumping" heat out of the interior to maintain a low temperature.

A refrigerator works by moving heat from the inside to the outside using a system of coils and a refrigerant. A pump circulates the refrigerant, which absorbs heat as it evaporates from a liquid into a gas inside the cooling coils of the fridge. This gas then flows into the condenser coils on the back or bottom, where it releases that heat into the surrounding air and turns back into a liquid. This continuous cycle keeps the interior cold by constantly pumping heat out of the cabinet.
